designs.runtimeCharacter: Seconds, interactive, laptop-only — no cluster, no parallelism, trivial memory. One .ab1 is ~100-300 kB and a nt+aa logo pair renders in well under a second; a full 12-24 sample sequencing plate batches in a few seconds, and the dominant cost is human time deciding each window's start/end/frame/orientation (the batching script exists to collapse that, not the compute). The AA collapse is 64 codon products per residue, i.e. negligible. The FlowJo .xls is ~100 rows and parses instantly. Everything is a foreground run in a notebook or a one-shot CLI; nothing needs a GPU, a queue, or $LAB_DATA_ROOT reference data.

critiques.revisedDescription: Guide-level statistics for CRISPR base-editing and prime-editing sensor screens, starting from a guide × sample count matrix: RPM (+1 pseudocount), log2 fold-change vs a T0-input or barcoding baseline, replicate mean/median/concordant-mean and z-scores, a bootstrap empirical null built from the library's safe- and non-targeting control guides, two-sided empirical p-values, Fisher's and Stouffer's combination, and BH FDR. House default for reporting: LFC_median + Fisher FDR < 0.1, |LFC| > 1. Produces `LFC-FDR/<screen>_LFC_FDR.csv`, the table every figure notebook reads. Use whenever asked to "calculate LFC and FDR", "run STEP9", "call hits", "is this guide significant", "did Tp53 drop out", "which guides are enriched or depleted in bone marrow / spleen / meninges", "which hits are tissue-specific", "the hit list looks too long", "nothing comes up significant", "why are all my p-values 1e-4", "why does MAGeCK call so many hits" (this is the deliberately conservative non-parametric alternative to MAGeCK, used because MAGeCK over-calls on individual-guide screens), "build the null from control guides", "add a new screen to the LFC pipeline", "re-run with spleen2 / bm2 excluded", "compare the hits between two screens", "where did ABE_OG_LFC_FDR.csv come from", or "the numbers changed since last run" (seed and n_bootstrap are pinned). Starts at the count matrix: FASTQ handling, CRISPResso, sensor extraction and building the count matrix are ngs-screen; designing the library and its control guides is library-design; styling the resulting plots is sci-plot; mouse↔human variant mapping is h2m_variant.

critiques.descriptionProblems: The description is unusually strong on trigger phrases — the quoted-phrase list ("model this human variant in mouse", "what is the mouse equivalent of TP53 R273H", "mouse-ify these mutations", "h2m this MAF") is the best part of the design and will fire on most real English requests. But it has concrete gaps: (1) ZERO Chinese. This user writes to Claude in Chinese constantly (the triggering request for this very workflow is Chinese). Descriptions are matched semantically but the embedding gets a large boost from literal phrase overlap; with 20+ English phrases and zero Chinese ones, the Chinese route is carried entirely by the gene-name token and "H2M". Add 5-8 Chinese phrases. (2) The word "ortholog" appears, but the standalone ortholog/transcript lookup job is buried as one phrase in a long list. That lightweight path deserves its own clause near the front, otherwise either the skill doesn't fire or it fires and overloads. (3) "H2M" the string is doing a lot of work and is ambiguous in this user's own world: human2mouse.com (the portal/database), the Nat Biotech paper, the h2m-public repo, and the bioh2m package. "run H2M" could mean "query the online database for what's already been modeled" — a cohort_query-shaped task. The description should disambiguate: this skill runs the package locally; it does not query the published H2M database. (4) The negative scope block is good but structurally risky. It names library-design, cohort_query, ngs-screen, survival_comut — if any of those skills is renamed or dropped, the description points at nothing. More importantly it is a *long* description (~250 words); the first sentence is what gets weighted most and it opens with "Models human genetic variants in the mouse genome (and the reverse) using the bioh2m package", which is good, but then spends the next 40 words on implementation detail (ortholog, canonical transcript, exact murine nucleotide change) before reaching a single user phrase. Front-load 3-4 user phrases into the first two sentences. (5) "which of these variants are class 0 vs class 3" assumes the user already knows H2M's class vocabulary. Most lab members won't. (6) No trigger for the single most common real entry point: a file.
missingCapabilities: Mouse-side genomic context for the downstream design step. The design hands library-design a CSV with chr_m/start_m/end_m/ref_seq_m/alt_seq_m — but PEGG's prime/base design needs the local mouse reference SEQUENCE around the site, and methods/library_design.ipynb shows the real workflow calls prime.genome_loader on the SAME mouse FASTA again inside the pegg env. The handoff as specified forces a second 3-minute multi-GB genome load in the next skill. The h2m skill already has records_m in memory and should optionally emit a flanking-sequence column (or a BED/FASTA of +/- 100 bp windows), which would let library-design skip the genome load entirely. This is the single highest-value missing capability and it is invisible from inside this skill's own boundary.

A no-genome 'quick answer' mode. h2m.query and get_tx_batch need no FASTA and no .db at all — they read packaged JSON. 'What's the mouse ortholog of KIT and its canonical transcript' should answer in under a second. As specified, every entry point routes through load_refs() and the user waits 3 minutes for a question that needed no reference data. scripts/h2m_paths.py as described eagerly loads all four objects; there is no lightweight path.

Reverse lookup from an amino-acid change in the mouse to the human equivalent at protein level, i.e. the m2h direction with coor='aa'. The design mentions m2h and mentions coor='aa' separately but never together, and the m2h + aa combination is what you need when a collaborator says 'our mouse line is Trp53 R172H, what human mutation is that' — an extremely common lab question.

Validation that the modeled mouse variant is actually editable before handing off. The design has param='BE' for base editing, but says nothing about the prime-editing feasibility question, and for BE it reports only whether the nucleotide change is a transition — not whether a PAM exists in range. That is library-design's job, but the skill should state the expected class-0/1 yield so the user knows roughly how many of their N variants will survive to design, rather than discovering it two skills later.

Caching of model results. A gene panel gets re-modeled from scratch every session (3 min load + alignment per transcript pair). A keyed cache (tx_id_h, tx_id_m, start, end, ref, alt, ver, param) -> result row under $LAB_DATA_ROOT would make iterative work on the same panel instant. The design explicitly caches the genome objects in a module global but never caches the far more expensive-to-recompute scientific output.

Status/class filtering semantics stated correctly (see descriptionProblems and overlap notes): the design asserts class 2 has no amino-acid-matched alternative and treats `status` as a clean bool, but in module.py class 2 is assigned at three sites (L861, L1689, L1907) and only one of them sets status=False — the other two reassign `error, statement` only, leaving whatever `status` was. Any instruction to 'filter status==True' will include or exclude class 2 inconsistently. The skill needs an explicit rule: filter on `class`, never on `status`.

A stated GENCODE/dict_tx version-compatibility check. The gotchas correctly note that a .db from a different GENCODE release surfaces as a bare KeyError inside GetTx, and that dict_tx_h.json is frozen at bioh2m 1.0.3 — but no script verifies the pairing. A 10-line preflight (pick one transcript from dict_tx_h, assert it exists in db_h) would convert a cryptic mid-run KeyError into a one-line setup error, and belongs in h2m_paths.py.

Nothing tells the user where to get the two .db files or the reference FASTAs in the first place. build_gencode_db.py builds the .db from a GTF, but the GENCODE v19/vM33 GTF URLs and the NCBI FASTA accessions are the actual blockers for a new lab member, and orthologs_canonical_tx.ipynb points at a Dropbox link that will rot. The skill should carry the exact download commands.
overlapsWith: library-design — the real seam, and it is drawn in the wrong place. h2m-variant claims it 'ends at the modeled variant coordinates' and hands over a CSV. But methods/library_design.ipynb (the lab's own ground truth) is a single notebook that imports `bioh2m as h2m` AND `from pegg import prime` and runs them together, re-loading the same mouse FASTA through prime.genome_loader. So the user's mental model is one continuous task ('model these in mouse and design the pegRNAs'), while the design splits it into two skills in two conda envs communicating by file. The env split is technically justified (pegg pins scikit-learn==1.1.1/numpy<2, bioh2m wants numpy>=1.24.2 — real and verified), but the skill must make the seam legible to the user rather than just declaring it. Without that chaining instruction Claude will fire one skill and stop, and the user will think it failed.

cohort_query — ambiguous on 'H2M' and on public-database readers. h2m-variant owns cbio_reader / clinvar_reader / vcf_reader / gnomAD CSV parsing, and names 'convert these GENIE/ClinVar/gnomAD variants to mouse coordinates' as a trigger. cohort_query presumably also reads GENIE/cBioPortal/COSMIC. 'Pull the TP53 hotspots from GENIE and model them in mouse' is genuinely both skills, in sequence. Worse, 'look up this variant in H2M' most naturally means the human2mouse.com database — which is cohort-query shaped — not a local package run. Both skills need a one-line boundary statement about who owns the public-database readers (recommendation: cohort_query owns frequency/recurrence questions and does the filtering; h2m-variant owns the MAF-normalization readers only as an input adapter when the user arrived with a raw file and no cohort question).

genotyping — low but non-zero. 'What's the mouse sequence at this variant / design primers to check the mouse allele' sits between h2m-variant (which knows the mouse coordinates and has the genome loaded) and genotyping. Should be explicitly assigned to genotyping, which the current negative-scope list does not mention at all — the design names library-design, cohort_query, ngs-screen, survival_comut as non-matches but omits genotyping and screen_stats.

sci-plot (an EXISTING skill, not in the planned set, and the design does notice this). h2m_figure.py produces the alignment plot and the design correctly says styling belongs to sci-plot. But sci-plot's own description explicitly claims 'h2m-style bars' and says to use it 'whenever writing, fixing, or restyling any Python plot... even when style isn't mentioned.' So 'make the H2M alignment figure' will plausibly pull sci-plot instead of h2m_variant. h2m.visualization is a fixed-layout plot from the package, not a restyle target — h2m-variant should state that this one figure is NOT a sci-plot deliverable, and sci-plot's 'h2m-style bars' means the class-distribution bar chart, which IS sci-plot's.
critiques.revisedDescription: Finds the mouse ortholog and canonical transcript, computes the exact murine nucleotide change reproducing the human protein effect, offers alternative codon strategies when the identical change fails, gates for base-editing compatibility (param='BE'), reports local homology confidence, and triages every variant into H2M class 0-6 (class 0/1 = orderable, 2 = effect not guaranteed, 3 = not modelable, 4/5 = your input is wrong). Also runs the reverse direction (mouse variant to human, m2h — e.g. "our line is Trp53 R172H, what human mutation is that") and paralog modeling within one species (h2h/m2m, SMARCA2 to SMARCA4). Includes fast no-genome ortholog and canonical-transcript lookup for single genes, and MAF normalization of cBioPortal/GENIE/ClinVar/gnomAD exports. Runs the local package in its own conda env; it does NOT query the published human2mouse.com database or cohort frequencies (cohort_query), does NOT design pegRNAs/sgRNAs (library-design — this skill ends by writing the modeled-variant CSV and handing it to that skill by name), and does NOT design genotyping primers (genotyping) or analyze sequencing data (ngs-screen).

overlapsWith: sci-plot — the sharpest collision, and it is with an ALREADY-INSTALLED skill, not a planned one. sci-plot's description claims volcano, z-score heatmap, correlation matrix, box+exact-P brackets, COSMIC-role semantic colors, and says to use it 'whenever writing, fixing, or restyling any Python plot ... even when style isn't mentioned'. survival_comut ships scripts/comut_plots.py (plot_ch_bubble ~130 lines + 12 private helpers, masked heatmaps, forest plots) and gene_freq.py (frequency bars + COSMIC role strip — a color map sci-plot already names). On 'make the co-occurrence volcano' or 'plot mutation frequency with COSMIC roles' both skills fire and the wrong one may win. Fix: survival_comut owns the STATISTICS and the plot-ready frames; it calls sci-plot for styling (fonts, pdf.fonttype=42, palettes). The genuinely non-obvious bits worth keeping locally are the double-sns.heatmap mask trick and the bubble layout — keep those, delete the font/palette/rc layer, and say in the description that figure STYLE comes from sci-plot.

cohort_query — the disclaimer ('not for querying raw public databases') is clean in principle but the design contradicts it. The SECONDARY source of truth, co-mutation-leukemia.ipynb, is named as the PREFERRED Fisher engine and it reads AACR-GENIE v17.0 from three hardcoded paths, filters Variant_Type=='SNP', and derives its own gene list from value_counts().iloc[:50]. That is a cohort_query job sitting inside survival_comut's engine. Worse, the description's 'works equally on AACR-GENIE or MSK-IMPACT pulls' actively invites GENIE requests here. Fix: survival_comut's input contract starts at an ALREADY-MATERIALIZED long-format table; cohort_query produces it. Say 'hand me the table cohort_query wrote' rather than claiming GENIE competence.

screen-stats — low collision risk but the stated boundary is drawn on the wrong axis. The doc separates by unit of analysis (patient vs guide), which is correct, but both skills do 'Fisher + BH FDR + volcano'. A bare 'run the FDR' or 'make the volcano' is ambiguous. The disambiguator a user actually types is the entity: patients/cohort/survival/OS vs guides/sgRNA/LFC/counts. Put those nouns in both descriptions, not the abstract phrase 'unit of analysis'.

survival_comut vs itself (gene_freq.py) — top_mutation_per_gene, the hotspot table, the frequency bars and the COSMIC role strip are cohort DESCRIPTIVES, not co-mutation or survival. 'what fraction of patients have DNMT3A' or 'plot mutation frequency' should not need a survival skill. Either split this into a cohort_describe skill or hand it to cohort_query, whose unit of analysis it shares.
missingCapabilities: THE 4-ARM STRATIFICATION — the most serious gap, and it is a silent-wrong-answer risk, not a convenience. Figure_2.R lines 574-609 builds a FOUR-level strata (STRATA1=1 focal, STRATA2=2 comparator, STRATA3=3 double; rowSums gives 0 = wild-type, 1 = focal-only, 2 = comparator-only, 6 = double) and then fits coxph(Surv(Time_to_OS, Censor) ~ STRATA_all) where STRATA_all = ifelse(STRATA==6, 6, 0) — i.e. DOUBLE vs EVERYONE ELSE, with survfit/ggsurvplot drawing the 4-arm KM. The notebook's build_pair_survival_dataset instead keeps only Double vs Driver_only and DROPS wild-type and focal-only patients. These answer different questions and give different HRs on the same data. The design doc flags the 2-arm contrast as a reporting hazard but never notes the R original uses a different contrast, and the published Figure 2 KM curves are 4-arm. A user who says 'redo the Figure 2 KM' gets the wrong plot with no warning. Ship BOTH contrasts as an explicit `contrast=` parameter ('double_vs_driver_only' | 'double_vs_rest' | 'four_arm'), make the four-arm KM a first-class output, and note the R guard is n_pts_both >= 10 where the notebook uses n >= 5 per arm.

MULTIVARIATE / ADJUSTED COX — the doc lists this as a gotcha ('should offer a covariates argument') but never puts it in coreCapabilities, scriptsNeeded or outputs, so it will not get built. fit_binary_cox is hardcoded to one covariate. For AML outcome this is not optional: NPM1 and FLT3-ITD are among the comparators AND are the dominant prognostic confounders, and Age/Sex/Cytogenetics/Risk/FAB are sitting unused in the table. I confirmed the notebook never touches them (zero occurrences of Cytogenetics, Risk, Sex, FAB, covariate, multivariate). Needs: a `covariates=[...]` passthrough to CoxPHFitter.fit, adjusted-HR columns alongside the univariate ones, and the schoenfeld/proportional-hazards check (lifelines check_assumptions) that a reviewer will demand.

A PATIENT-LEVEL ONCOPRINT / co-mutation waterfall. Verified absent from CH.ipynb (zero hits for oncoprint, comut, waterfall, upset — despite upsetplot being installed and listed in envDependencies, which suggests it was intended). This is the single most-requested co-mutation figure in clinical genomics and the natural reply to 'show me the co-mutation pattern'. Without it the skill answers 'are they exclusive' with a p-value but cannot show the pattern.

REGRESSION TESTING against the fixtures it already names. The doc identifies the anchors (DNMT3A/NPM1 OR 5.3769112, p 5.3157e-60, n_double 345; DNMT3A + NPM1 HR 1.2275637, 0.9855174-1.5290572) and I verified all of them against the CSVs, plus 15/200 floored ORs, 10 focal genes, and 107 of 200 pairs surviving the n>=5 filter. But no test script is in scriptsNeeded. Since the plan deliberately CHANGES the engine (safe_log_or replacing the 0.06982398 literal, vectorized Fisher replacing per-pair crosstab), a tests/test_survival_comut.py asserting p_value and n_double reproduce exactly while odds_ratio changes only on the 15 or_floored cells is what separates a refactor from a silent regression. Add the 107/200 count as a fixture too — it pins the n>=5 guard.

PER-PAIR SKIP ACCOUNTING as a returned artifact, not just a record. The doc asks for n_tested/skipped_reason but neither appears in the stated output columns of pairwise_ch_driver_survival_summary.csv. 93 of 200 pairs are MISSING from that file, not non-significant. Any downstream .pivot yields NaN cells that read as null results. Ship a companion pairs_skipped.csv (ch_gene, driver_gene, n_double, n_driver_only, reason) and make every heatmap distinguish not-tested from not-significant visually, the way only CELL 44 currently does.

CENSORING AND COHORT SANITY REPORT. Time_to_OS is in DAYS (max 6780) and nothing in the name says so; the doc catches the /365 trap but offers no provisioning of the checks as output. A one-page cohort QC the user can read before trusting anything: n patients, n events vs censored, median follow-up, Censor level check, Time_to_OS magnitude verdict, per-gene patient counts, and which Subset levels were kept. Cheap, and it is what stops the days-vs-years and the 'is 1 really death' errors from reaching a figure.

COSMIC CANCER GENE CENSUS PROVISIONING. I confirmed $LAB_DATA_ROOT/PublicDatabase/COSMIC/ holds only Cosmic_MutantCensus_Tsv_v99_GRCh37 — the Cancer Gene Census is genuinely not there, and $LAB_DATA_ROOT is unset in this shell. The doc says the skill should 'say what to download'; that needs to be an actual documented fetch step (COSMIC login, which file, where it lands) or gene_freq.py's role strip is dead on arrival for everyone including its author.

GLOBAL vs WITHIN-FAMILY FDR AS A SIDE-BY-SIDE. The doc makes the correction level a parameter, which is right, but the actionable form is to emit BOTH q columns (q_within_focal, q_global) in cooccurrence_ch_vs_top20.csv and print which one each figure used into the figure itself. I verified the within-focal transform is exactly as described and that Figure_2.R line 451 adjusts globally — so the notebook's published q values are not the R paper's q values. A reviewer comparing the two will find the discrepancy before the user does.
critiques.descriptionProblems:
"The description is genuinely good by this repo's own standard — it does not restate the title, it names real file and column names (final_data_matrix.RData, Sample/Gene/Time_to_OS/Censor), it carries ~14 quoted trigger phrases, and it ends with an explicit not-for clause naming the three neighbours. That is better than most. Five concrete problems remain.

(1) NO CHINESE DOMAIN TERMS, and this user works bilingually — the relayed request that spawned this review is itself in Chinese. The repo's own docs/writing-a-skill.md says 'naming the domain terms both ways helps' and this description names none. The directory holds co-occurrence.pdf, cooccurrence_bubble.pdf, cooccurrence_heatmap.pdf, survival_bubble.pdf, survival_heatmap.pdf, survival_summary_v2/v3/v4.pdf, top20_specific_mutations.pdf, DNMT3A_RAD21_FLT3ITD_KM.pdf — the v2/v3/v4 series is direct evidence of repeated 'regenerate that figure' requests. 'regenerate survival_heatmap.pdf' currently MISSES. These filenames are the highest-precision triggers available and none are in the description.

(3) THE ADJUSTED-MODEL VOCABULARY IS ABSENT. 'multivariate cox', 'adjust for age', 'add covariates', 'cytogenetic risk' all miss — and this is exactly where the skill is weakest anyway, so a miss here compounds a capability gap into a silent wrong answer.

(4) 'Figure 2' IS NOT NAMED. Figure_2.R and Figure_2.ipynb are the provenance of this entire analysis; The description must claim Figure 2 and the skill body must flag the contrast difference.

(5) THE NEIGHBOUR DISCLAIMER NAMES THE WRONG NEIGHBOUR. It disclaims h2m-variant, screen-stats and cohort_query but says nothing about sci-plot, which is already installed, already claims 'volcano' and 'heatmap', and already instructs Claude to prefer it for any matplotlib figure 'even when style isn't mentioned'. Meanwhile the description's own 'works equally on AACR-GENIE or MSK-IMPACT pulls' contradicts its cohort_query disclaimer by advertising database competence the skill is explicitly not supposed to have. Drop that clause or restate it as 'on a table cohort_query already pulled'.

Minor: whenToUse leans on the abstract phrase 'unit of analysis is a patient', which is the right concept but not a phrase any user types. The discriminating nouns (patient, cohort, survival, OS, prognosis vs guide, sgRNA, LFC, counts) should appear in the description itself, where the trigger decision is actually made."
critiques.revisedDescription: Takes any long-format table with Sample, Gene, Time_to_OS (days) and Censor columns; the MetaAML CH cohort is final_data_matrix.RData. The unit is a PATIENT: for guide- or variant-level LFC/FDR use screen-stats, for pulling the cohort out of GENIE/COSMIC/cBioPortal in the first place use cohort_query (hand this skill the table it wrote), and for annotating or humanizing variants use h2m_variant. Computes the statistics and the plot-ready frames; figure fonts, palettes and PDF export come from sci-plot. Never reports \"significant\" without naming the threshold, the correction and the contrast."

overlapsWith: survival_comut — the worst overlap in the set, and it is a naming collision, not just a topical one. survival_comut's name literally contains 'comut'; cohort_query claims Fisher co-mutation testing, volcano, and OR heatmap as core capabilities. A user who types 'co-mutation volcano' (a verbatim trigger phrase in cohort_query's description) has no way to land deterministically. Worse, the split cuts one real analysis in half: CH.ipynb is cited as cohort_query's sourceOfTruth (cells 6, 9, 28), but that notebook's co-occurrence (cells 11/13/16/43) and its Kaplan-Meier (cells 34-36) run on the SAME dataframe derived from final_data_matrix.RData — and the design hands RData to survival_comut while keeping co-mutation here. Reproducing CH.ipynb would require both skills and a schema cohort_query cannot read. Fix: give Fisher/OR/volcano/heatmap wholly to survival_comut (rename it comut_survival), and let cohort_query emit the patient x gene binary matrix as a handoff artifact. cohort_query then owns 'which patients carry what', survival_comut owns 'what does carrying it associate with'.

library-design — the description claims the trigger 'get me a MAF table of B-ALL variants to design a library against', which is phrased as a design request. The honest boundary (frequency ranking here, designability verdict in library-design) is correctly stated in gotcha 12, but it lives in gotchas where the router never reads it. The ITD_MAX_INS_NT = 21 / RTT<=30 / min_RHA_size=8 material in scriptsNeeded and sourceOfTruth (cell 74) is library-design's constraint model appearing in cohort_query's spec.

h2m-variant — mostly clean, but cohort_query claims cells 108-120 including 'the rename map Start_Position->start ... Tumor_Seq_Allele2->alt_seq'. That rename is h2m's input adapter. Both skills owning it means two copies that can drift. cohort_query should emit cBioPortal column names (as outputs says) and stop there; h2m-variant owns the rename.

sci-plot (already shipped) — coreCapabilities 7, 9, 10 and scripts/plots.py bake in rcParams, COSMIC role colors, and fonttype-42 PDF export. scriptsNeeded says styling 'should delegate to the sci-plot skill', but sci-plot's description already fires on 'volcano', 'z-score heatmap', 'COSMIC roles', and 'correlation matrix' — so cohort_query's plotting capabilities re-advertise what a live skill claims. Keep the data assembly here; let sci-plot own appearance, and say so in the description, not only in scriptsNeeded.
missingCapabilities: Structural variants and fusions — the single biggest gap, and the description's own trigger list exposes it. 'how many AML patients have FLT3-ITD' is listed as a firing phrase, and the B-ALL cohort is defined by 'with t(9;22);BCR-ABL1' subtypes. But I checked GENIE v17: data_sv.txt is a wholly separate table (Sample_Id, Site1_Hugo_Symbol, Site2_Hugo_Symbol, Site1_Position, SV_Status) and the MAF has NO fusion rows — Variant_Classification over 200k rows is Missense/Nonsense/Splice/Frameshift/Intron only. data_sv.txt is mentioned once, parenthetically, in inputs ('plus data_clinical_patient.txt and data_sv.txt for SV work'), and no capability, script, or output ever touches it. So the advertised BCR-ABL1 and ETV6-RUNX1 queries return zero rows and the skill cannot tell the user why. Note FLT3-ITD does partly live in the MAF as In_Frame_Ins (1169 rows in my sample), so an ITD query half-works — which is worse than failing, because the user gets a plausible undercount. Either add scripts/sv.py with the patient-prefix join from 02_filter_sv_mutations.py, or remove FLT3-ITD/fusions from the trigger list and make the skill say 'fusions are in data_sv.txt, not covered'.

Copy-number alteration — ALL B-ALL and AML cohorts are driven by CDKN2A/IKZF1 deletions and iAMP21 (3 samples in the detailed breakdown I pulled). GENIE v17.0 ships data_cna_hg19.seg; no data_CNA.txt in that directory. 'Which genes co-mutate with TP53' silently means 'co-mutate by point mutation only', and the output never says so. At minimum this needs a stated scope limit on every co-mutation result, since a negative co-occurrence result for a CNA-driven gene is uninterpretable without it.

Patient-level clinical covariates. data_clinical_patient.txt is loaded in the source notebook and listed in inputs, but nothing uses it. A biologist asking 'is DNMT3A R882H enriched in older patients' or 'what is the sex split' gets nothing — and GENIE's AGE_AT_SEQ_REPORT is in data_clinical_sample.txt, which the skill already reads. This is cheap to add and the omission looks accidental.

VAF / clonality. t_alt_count and t_ref_count are in every MAF. For a CH skill — where the whole distinction between clonal hematopoiesis and overt AML is VAF — not exposing VAF is a conceptual hole, not a convenience gap. 'Is this a CH-range variant' is unanswerable.

Frequency as a rate, with a confidence interval. Every output is a raw 'count'. Nobody reports '68 patients'; they report '0.03% (68/198,000, 95% CI ...)'. gotcha 6 correctly insists the denominator must be carried, then the outputs spec carries only the numerator plus a provenance line. The denominator should be a COLUMN (n_cohort, freq, ci_low, ci_high), not prose, so it survives into a figure or a table a reviewer reads.

Per-patient collapse as a first-class switch. gotcha 7 identifies the bug precisely and even gives the fix ('-'.join(id.split('-')[:3])), then leaves the resolution as 'Decide, and state on the output'. Undecided in the spec means decided ad hoc at runtime. filter_variants' per_sample=True does sample-level nunique; the 02/03 scripts do patient-level. These give different numbers on GENIE, where one patient commonly has primary + relapse samples. Pick patient-level as the default, name the column n_patients, and offer --per-sample.

Multi-version comparison. The registry lists six GENIE versions (v13.1-v18.0, and I confirmed v13.1/v14.0/v15.0/v16.1/v17.0/v18.0 all on disk) but no capability compares across them. 'Did this variant get more common in v18 than v17' is the natural reason to keep six versions, and it is also the only defense against a reviewer asking why the paper says v17.

A stable COSMIC Census location. gotcha 11 says the skill 'should look there and only there' under $LAB_DATA_ROOT/PublicDatabase/COSMIC/ — but I checked: that directory contains only Cosmic_MutantCensus_Tsv_v99_GRCh37/, and the Census_all csv exists in FOUR analysis repos (B-ALL-in-vivo-base-editing, SG-B-ALL-in-vivo-base-editing, PE7-mouse-multiplexed-editing, first-year/...) and nowhere under COSMIC/. So get_cosmic_role() fails on day one. The skill needs a provisioning step (docs/data-layout.md already exists in the repo for this) or it must ship the resolver with a fallback and a loud warning.

A gene-symbol alias layer. GENIE uses older HUGO symbols for some genes (PTPN11 appears in PROTEIN_AA where a user may type SHP2; MLL vs KMT2A matters for the B-ALL t(v;11q23.3) subtype). A silent empty result from a renamed gene is indistinguishable from a true zero.
critiques.descriptionProblems:
"The description is far better than most — it names real cohorts, real versions, and eleven verbatim trigger phrases, so it will not fail the way a title-restating description fails. Its problems are different and more specific.

1. LENGTH DEFEATS IT. At ~1,900 characters it is roughly 3x pegrna-oligo's shipped description. The decisive trigger phrases sit in the final third, after four sentences of implementation detail ('collapses recurrent variants into one row per variant with a per-patient sample count', 'binary matrix', 'Benjamini-Hochberg FDR'). The mechanism prose is what the router has to wade through to reach the phrases that actually match user language.

2. NO CHINESE, AND THIS USER WRITES CHINESE. The request that spawned this whole skill set is in Chinese. Every trigger phrase is English. Note sci-plot and pegrna-oligo are also English-only, so this is a set-wide fix — but cohort_query is the one most likely to be asked about in Chinese, because it is the clinical/reading-oriented skill rather than a bench protocol. THE STRONGEST REAL TRIGGER IS ABSENT: a bare gene-and-variant string. Biologists type 'DNMT3A R882H' or 'IDH2 R140Q?' with no verb. Nothing in the description says a bare variant name should fire this skill. Relatedly, every example uses p.-prefixed or bare protein changes, but users also paste genomic coordinates ('chr2:25457242') and rsIDs — gotcha 10 shows the author knows HGVSp strings are non-canonical, yet the description advertises only one input shape.

4. 'cohort_query' IS NOT A WORD A BIOLOGIST USES. Compare to anneal / gga / sci-plot, which are lab vocabulary. Nobody will invoke this by name, so the description carries 100% of the routing load — which makes problems 1-3 cost more than they would for a well-named skill.

5. OVERCLAIMS. 'AACR-GENIE (v13.1–v18.0)' reads as six supported cohorts, but every verified code path and all five gotcha sample counts are v17.0-specific; v18.0 column stability is unverified. And 'MSK-IMPACT (msk_impact_2017)' appears in the headline with zero supporting capability, script, or gotcha anywhere in the spec — it is a path in the registry, nothing more. Advertising an unexercised cohort means the skill fires confidently on 'what's the frequency in MSK-IMPACT' and then improvises.

6. ONE FACTUAL ERROR IN coreCapabilities (not the description, but it would ship): capability 2 says 'Restrict a cohort to a disease by CANCER_TYPE or CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED ... lifted from ch_aml_mutation_list.ipynb cell 7 (MSK-HEME AML, 296 samples)'. Cell 7 filters CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED == 'Acute Myeloid Leukemia' only. Given gotcha 1 is entirely about a 1.6x sample-count error from confusing exactly these two columns, miscrediting the source cell is the one error in this spec most likely to propagate. (I verified gotcha 1 itself is exactly right: on v17.0, CANCER_TYPE == 'B-Lymphoblastic Leukemia/Lymphoma' gives 1459, CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED exact-match gives 886, CANCER_TYPE at column index 6, ~11 detailed subtypes.)

The negative clauses ('It does NOT convert variants to mouse...') are good practice and should stay, but they cannot resolve the survival_comut collision, because survival_comut is named in the exclusion list while co-mutation is claimed as a capability — the exclusion contradicts the claim."
critiques.revisedDescription: "Look up how often a mutation or gene is mutated in real cancer patients, in which cancer types, and in how many — from AACR-GENIE v17.0 (pan-cancer, ~200k samples, GRCh37), MSK-HEME (heme_msk_impact_2022), MSK-IMPACT 2017, and COSMIC (Cancer Gene Census roles + MutantCensus v99). Produces a per-variant frequency table with its denominator (n_patients out of cohort N, with the disease filter named), a per-gene ranking annotated with COSMIC oncogene/TSG role, the top recurrent mutations in a gene, per-gene mutation-position profiles in two cohorts side by side, and a patient x gene binary matrix for downstream co-mutation or survival analysis. Falls back from a disease cohort to pan-cancer GENIE when a variant is absent and says which cohort each hit came from. Columns come out in cBioPortal/MAF form so the table feeds straight into h2m-variant or library_design. Not for: human-to-mouse conversion (h2m-variant), guide or pegRNA design and designability (library-design, pegrna-oligo), screen readouts (ngs-screen, screen-stats), or Fisher co-mutation / mutual-exclusivity testing and Cox/Kaplan-Meier survival (survival_comut — this skill hands it the binary matrix). Point mutations and indels only: fusions and rearrangements live in data_sv.txt and copy-number in the CNA files, neither of which this covers."

overlapsWith: pegrna-oligo (shipped, not planned): the boundary is asserted twice but is wrong in both directions. library-design claims to end at "the pooled oligo table" and emits `pegRNA_oligo`/`gRNA_oligo` via prime_oligo_generator/base_oligo_generator; pegrna-oligo's shipped description says it turns "a PEGG/PRIDICT pegRNA design table into everything needed to order" including "an IDT oligo order sheet". A user typing "turn my PEGG designs into oligos I can order" matches both verbatim. The real discriminator (pooled synthesis oligo = one long sequence per pegRNA for chip/array synthesis, vs Golden Gate = three annealed duplex oligo pairs ordered individually) appears in neither description in words a user would type. library-design must say "pooled/array synthesis, one sequence per pegRNA" and "not for IDT order sheets or individually ordered Golden Gate oligos".

ngs-screen: library-design owns `sensor=True`, sensor_length, sensor_orientation, sensor_wt/sensor_alt, sensor_error and `prime.sensor_viz`. ngs-screen is "Sensor screen FASTQ -> counts -> CRISPResso2". Neither whenToUse distinguishes designing a sensor cassette from reading sensor amplicons. Worse, the reference amplicons CRISPResso2 needs are produced here, and that handoff is unnamed in both skills.

h2m-variant: library-design's inputs section embeds the entire H2M->MAF rename block and `tx_id_m`, and scripts/prep_input.py owns `maf_from_h2m`. Whichever skill owns the rename must own it once; right now library-design claims it unilaterally.

screen-stats: controls.py here builds safe-targeting and non-targeting arms and stamps `classification`; screen-stats' README description says its bootstrap null is "pooled from safe-targeting and non-targeting control guides". That column name and its allowed values are an inter-skill contract specified in only one place — and incompletely: the stated values are 'variant' / 'safe-targeting control' / 'AAVS1-targeting control', with no label for non-targeting guides, which are the main null source.

sci-plot: library_report.py "imports the sci-plot skill's kdplot". sci-plot claims to fire for any Python plot for this user "even when style isn't mentioned". A cross-skill Python import is fragile under the symlink install (install.sh symlinks skills into ~/.claude/skills) and should be a declared dependency with a graceful fallback, not an import.
missingCapabilities: Resume from checkpoint. The design states scoring is 6.5 h + 4.4 h, that it lives only in kernel memory, and that "a NameError in a later cell once destroyed a completed 6.5 h run" — then ships no resume path: no scripts/resume.py, no --checkpoint flag on design_prime.py, no manifest of which mutations are already scored. The most expensive failure the gotchas describe has no remedy anywhere in scriptsNeeded. This is the single biggest gap.

Cost/time estimate before launching. runtimeCharacter has every needed number (0.2155 s/pegRNA/worker, ~20 s JIT per worker, window 5->3,928 / 10->19,440 / 15->87,984 / 30->1,334,448 pegRNAs per variant) but no scripts/estimate_cost.py.

Order-size / budget as an input. The skill offers pegRNAs_per_mut and a post-hoc coverage-vs-cutoff curve, but no function solving the inverse: given a pegRNA budget and a mutation list, allocate per mutation while keeping every mutation covered. The gotchas already explain why naive overall-rank capping fails (plain and bystander scores are not on one scale), so the correct logic is understood and simply not exposed.

Round-trip verification of the assembled oligo. audit_bystanders.py checks that the RTT translates silently; nothing checks the final `pegRNA_oligo` string — that the embedded protospacer matches the Protospacer column, that the extension is RTT_PBS in the right orientation, that adapters and scaffold are intact, and critically that concatenation did not create a BsmBI CGTCTC at a junction. contains_RE_site is computed on components before assembly (verified: other_filtration runs on RTT_PBS/Protospacer), so a junction-created site passes every stated filter and kills the Golden Gate.

Off-target / specificity assessment. The skill scores on-target efficiency three ways (Azimuth, PEGG2, OptiPrime) and never asks whether a protospacer is unique in the genome. For a mouse library this is a routine ordering decision and a routine reviewer question. Either a chrom_dict exact-match count or an explicit out-of-scope statement is needed; silence reads as coverage.

Per-variant dropout ledger as a real output. "why did my variant drop out of the library" is advertised as a trigger, but no output or script produces a table naming the stage that killed each variant. The gotchas enumerate at least eight independent silent-drop stages: not a SNP (run_base auto_SNP_filter, verified base.py:298), chromosome absent from chrom_dict, no eligible PAM, min_RHA_size, cds_valid False, sensor too small, contains_polyT_terminator, contains_RE_site, the per-mutation cap, and optiprime_cutoff. Advertising the question without emitting the table is the gap most likely to be hit in actual use.

Mouse non-targeting guides. Verified: library.py:403 nontargeting_guides reads non_targeting_human_prime.csv unconditionally with no organism argument, and clamps >1000 with a print (library.py:424-426). The mouse source ships unprocessed as non_targeting_unformatted_mus.txt. Every library this skill is built around is mouse. The gotcha states the limitation and offers no path; processing that file once is a concrete deliverable this skill should own, since screen-stats depends on those guides for its null.

Verification for plain indel and ONP/DNP/TNP designs. Variant_Type accepts DNP/TNP/ONP/INS/DEL/INDEL and pegg 3.1 is credited with "the indel reading-frame fix", but the only verifier is restricted to bystander rows. The designs the 3.1 fix actually touches go unchecked, and 20 of the 44 CH/AML variants are frameshift, nonsense or in-frame indels.
critiques.descriptionProblems: The description is unusually rich in trigger phrases and will fire reliably on explicit PEGG/pegRNA requests. Its problems are specificity, language coverage, and two outright factual errors. 1. About 190 words, much of it API-name bait. "run prime.run", "run run_base", "PEGG2_Score" are typed only by someone who already knows the library and has therefore already decided to use it. They consume the scarcest token budget in the repo and buy almost no recall. The phrases that earn their place are the natural-language ones: "design guides for these mutations", "which PBS and RTT lengths should I enumerate", "why did my variant drop out of the library". 2. Zero Chinese, in a repo whose author works bilingually — this very session's request was in Chinese. The repo's own docs/writing-a-skill.md says "If people ask in Chinese as well as English... naming the domain terms both ways helps" — the design ignores its own house rule. Six to eight of these suffice. 3. The highest-frequency real phrasings are missing. A biologist types "design guides to knock in Dnmt3a R882H in mouse", "make a prime editing library for these 40 mutations", "which pegRNAs should I order", "pick the best 50 pegRNAs per mutation", "add controls to my library", "how many oligos is this". Only "make me a CH/AML pegRNA library" is covered. Notably "prime editing" as a bare phrase — the term the field actually uses — appears nowhere; "pegRNA" carries the entire load. 4. The negative boundary is in whenToUse, which is not the trigger surface. The repo's docs are explicit: "The description is the whole trigger mechanism. It is the only text Claude sees when deciding whether to load the skill." All disambiguation against pegrna-oligo, ngs-screen and h2m-variant sits in a field read only after the choice is made. The one negative clause that did reach the description ("hand its output to pegrna-oligo") is the right pattern and should be joined by a sensor one and an h2m one. 5. "audit that designed bystanders really are synonymous" triggers a capability that cannot be reached independently. audit_bystanders.py needs seq_start, which the gotchas correctly note exists only on the cBioPortal path. A user who designed from WT_ALT and asks "check my bystanders are silent" loads this skill and hits an unexplained failure. Either the trigger says cBioPortal-designed, or the script fails by name. 6. FACTUAL ERROR reaching the user. The gotcha "A non-NGG PAM prints a warning" is true only for prime — verified at prime.py:1831-1832 (`if PAM != 'NGG': print('Warning: Efficiency predictions on non-NGG PAMs are un-tested')`). grep over base.py finds no PAM warning at all; the only near-miss is a dead comment at base.py:390 ("#MAYBE LIMIT THIS TO ONLY NGG PAMS???"). The validated base-editing profile in this very design is PAM='NG', so the one configuration the user will actually run is the one with no warning, documented as warning. Split the gotcha: prime warns, base is silent, and OnTarget_Azimuth_Score is unvalidated on both. 7. SECOND FACTUAL ERROR, in inputs. bystander.add_cds_to_variants defaults to tx_column='tx_id_h' (verified bystander.py:1340), not 'tx_id_m'. coreCapabilities shows tx_column='tx_id_m' without flagging that the human default silently applies otherwise — a KeyError on a mouse-only table, and silently the wrong species' reading frame on an H2M table carrying both columns. For a mouse-first skill this belongs in gotchas, not buried in an argument example. 8. Why too-broad, concretely. Fourteen capabilities, eleven scripts and twenty-five gotchas is defensible as one skill: prime and base genuinely share input formatting, chrom_dict, sensors, controls, filters and oligo assembly, and splitting them duplicates all of it. What does not belong is OptiPrime. It is a separate Python 3.11 environment with an incompatible numpy, a separate repo clone, two env vars, its own availability probe (optiprime.py:79), its own group-validation correctness trap (VALID_GROUPS, optiprime.py:57-62), and roughly 11 of the skill's 11.1 hours of runtime; six of twenty-five gotchas are OptiPrime's alone. That is its own skill — optiprime_score: score an existing pegRNA table, validate the group against the 12 keys, estimate wall time, shard, checkpoint, resume — which library-design calls with optiprime=False by default. Splitting makes library-design a minutes-long reproducible design skill and isolates the long-running, env-fragile, resume-needing part in the one place resume can actually be built.
critiques.revisedDescription: Design prime-editing pegRNA and base-editing sgRNA libraries from a variant table with PEGG — enumerate PAM sites, RTT and PBS lengths, pick ABE vs CBE, attach sensor cassettes, add silent-bystander and synonymous-codon designs, add safe-targeting / non-targeting / AAVS1 controls, and emit the pooled synthesis oligo table plus a per-variant dropout ledger. Takes a MAF-format or H2M-derived variant table plus a reference genome; needs Python 3.9/3.10 with scikit-learn==1.1.1 and numpy<2. Ends at the pooled synthesis oligo table (one sequence per pegRNA, for chip synthesis) — for an IDT sheet of individually ordered Golden Gate oligos use `pegrna-oligo`; for human→mouse variant modeling use `h2m-variant`; for reading sensor amplicons out of screen FASTQs use `ngs-screen`.

overlapsWith: ngs-screen — direct functional overlap on the user's actual question ("did the edit work", "what's my editing efficiency"); the stated boundary is FASTQ vs .ab1, which is a file-format distinction users do not voice. Both answer "quantify editing at R248Q". Disambiguation must be bidirectional: ngs-screen's description must say "not .ab1/Sanger" or this one-sided carve-out does nothing. Also real risk of the reverse error — someone with amplicon FASTQ saying "call the edit" lands here.

sci-plot — the entire flow half is three matplotlib bar panels. sci-plot's description claims "whenever writing, fixing, or restyling ANY Python plot ... even when style isn't mentioned" and its gallery already has "Stacked single bar with counts". The flow panels arguably belong as sci-plot gallery recipes, leaving genotyping the parsing + count math.
library-design / pegrna-oligo — mild: design-the-edit vs validate-the-edit. Already handled by the whenToUse line; low risk since those skills are anchored on oligo/order/clone vocabulary.

screen-stats — marginal: the flow half computes percentages and fold expansion with no statistics, while screen-stats owns "compute the stats". If a user asks "is the LSK expansion significant?" neither clearly owns it.
missingCapabilities: Automatic window/frame/strand location by aligning the AB1-called sequence (or the parallel .seq FASTA the design dismisses as 'NOT needed') against a user-supplied expected amplicon or CDS, returning start/end/frame/reverse_complement and the offset. The design explicitly punts this to the user, yet runtimeCharacter names 'human time deciding each window's start/end/frame/orientation' as the dominant cost — so the skill hands back the only hard part. This one addition also neutralizes the three worst gotchas (silent wrong-codon window, undetectable frame shift, wrong reverse_complement) and the off-by-N from the leading N-run in real reads (KP_Sort-p53_F.ab1 starts NNNNNNNNN).

A matched WT/unedited control trace comparison. Peak-height proportions are uncalibrated (the design says so in gotcha 9), so they are only interpretable as a difference from an unedited trace at the same position. call_edit() takes no control argument; add --control to subtract per-position background before reporting an edited fraction.

Indel / trace-quality refusal. Gotcha 10 states an indel makes everything downstream of the edit uninterpretable, but nothing in scriptsNeeded detects it. Add a guard (rising mixed-base fraction after the expected cut site, or low phred over the window from record.letter_annotations['phred_quality']) that makes the skill refuse to report a number rather than print a confident wrong one.

Clone genotyping: homozygous / heterozygous / WT / unedited call per clone across a plate, with a threshold and an explicit 'ambiguous' class. This is the single most common real request ('I sequenced my clones, which ones are homozygous?') and is a thin wrapper on call_edit, yet it appears in neither coreCapabilities nor the trigger vocabulary.

A .seq / FASTA-only path. Declared unnecessary, but it is the cheapest way to verify a window is in the right place, and it is the only input available when a collaborator sends sequences without traces.

Replicate statistics on the flow side. There are three samples and the code only ever takes .mean() — no SD, no n, no error bars, no per-sample dots. This contradicts the lab's own sci-plot house style (bars with SD caps and replicate dots). Also: carry #Cells through so a gate with n=4 of 260 (Sample 1 LSK CD150+ CD34-) is annotated or refused.

.fcs support, or an explicit alternative. Declared unsupported; readfcs/FlowCytometryTools is a pip install, and users who have lost the FlowJo workspace have only the .fcs. At minimum state the fallback rather than just refusing.
Knock-in / HDR and base-editing-window vocabulary and readouts ('knock-in efficiency', 'KI', 'HDR', 'what's my A>G conversion at position 5'). The skill computes exactly this but names none of it.
critiques.descriptionProblems:
"It would mostly trigger, but it has four real defects plus two factual errors that would be ported into the skill body as false lab knowledge.

STRUCTURE: the first ~40 words after the title are implementation mechanism ('base proportions directly from the ABI trace channels (DATA9-12 at PLOC1 peak positions)'), which no user will ever type. The phrases that actually fire are buried in sentence three. Front-load the trigger surface, demote the mechanism.

TWO SKILLS IN ONE DESCRIPTION: Sanger .ab1 and FlowJo .xls share no format, no library (biopython+logomaker vs xlrd), no concept and no output. Carrying both vocabularies dilutes both, and the flow half competes directly with sci-plot. 11 coreCapabilities / 7 scripts / 18 gotchas split roughly half and half. Split into sanger_edit and flow_readout.

MISSING TRIGGERS (English): 'which clones are homozygous', 'heterozygous', 'genotype the colonies', 'screen my clones', 'is this a knockout', 'FACS' (many people say FACS, never 'flow'), 'HSC frequency', 'immunophenotype', 'knock-in efficiency', 'HDR', 'conversion efficiency', 'my sequencing came back'. The clone-genotyping gap is the worst: 'I sequenced my clones, which ones are homozygous?' is the commonest real request and matches nothing.

MISSING TRIGGERS (Chinese): per the repo's own docs/writing-a-skill.md ('naming the domain terms both ways helps'), there is no Chinese at all. Checked against the filenames: 4_R273C_RV_N-P1_RV.ab1 (reverse, False), 6_R273H_RV-1_RV.ab1 (reverse, False), 5_R248Q_FW_N-P2_FW.ab1 (forward, True), 10_R270C_FW-4_FW.ab1 (forward, True), 12_R270H_FW-4_FW.ab1 (forward, True). The mapping is the exact inverse of the primer name in EVERY case — perfectly systematic, not inconsistent. The explanation is that TP53 sits on the minus strand, so an FW-primer read is antisense to the CDS and needs RC. Rewrite as: 'for a minus-strand gene such as TP53, reverse_complement=True goes with the FW primer read' — the design's conclusion (determine orientation from sequence, not filename) is right but its evidence is inverted.

FACTUAL ERROR 2: 'logomaker is not installed in ANY conda env on this machine ... The notebook's very first line therefore fails'. logomaker 0.8.7 IS importable from /usr/bin/python3 (system Python 3.9, what `python3` resolves to), so the notebook runs as written. Confirmed absent from all six conda envs (base, myenv, pegg, pegg3, pegg_env, stat_env). The correct warning is 'works only in system Python 3.9; absent from every conda env, so it breaks the moment anyone activates pegg_env or moves to the server' — and pin it (0.8.x, pre-1.0).

THIRD PROBLEM, not in the description but fatal to shipping: sourceOfTruth conflates two datasets. The .ab1 files in the repo are mouse KP_Pre/KP_Sort/PK_Pre x Kras/p53 x F/R; all 15 notebook invocation blocks point at /Users/kexindong/Desktop/.../A549_P53Mutations_... human TP53 reads that are NOT in the repo. So there is no known-good start/end for any file a user will have, and no Sanger regression fixture can ship until someone records the correct window for one KP/PK read. The flow fixture by contrast is genuine (Sample 1 LSK 6.7827 from 9.83 x 69.0 reproduced from flow_summary.csv).

Also contradictory: scriptsNeeded says lift sanger_weblogo VERBATIM, then separately says ab1_trace.py should 'factor out (and reuse inside sanger_weblogo)' its first 15 lines. Pick one — keep sanger_logo.py verbatim as the reference and let ab1_trace.py be an independent re-expression, with a test asserting the two agree on KP_Sort-p53_F.ab1."
critiques.revisedDescription: Call genome-editing outcomes from Sanger .ab1 traces — editing efficiency, bystander edits, and homozygous/heterozygous/WT clone calls at a codon, as a number and as nucleotide and amino-acid sequence logos. Reads per-base proportions from the raw ABI trace channels rather than the single called base, so a mixed or partially edited position is quantified instead of eyeballed; locates the window by aligning the read against the expected amplicon or CDS so start/end, frame and strand are derived, not guessed; collapses codons into per-residue amino-acid proportions with real residue numbering; batches a whole plate from a variant table. Compares against a matched unedited control and refuses to report a percentage when the trace is indel-disrupted or low-quality. NOT for FASTQ — amplicon NGS editing quantification is ngs-screen/CRISPResso2; NOT for designing the edit (library-design, pegrna-oligo); NOT for flow cytometry (flow_readout). Bundling it here shares no format, library, concept or output with Sanger and puts the description in direct competition with sci-plot.]
